digest.component_or_area: reconciler rich-text send-path cutover + baseline state machine
propositions: Cloud and DC send paths must cut to rich codecs (ADF and rendered wiki respectively) with state-based echo suppression via baseline diff, not codec idempotence, because DC's codec is lossy.

An 8-byte inline `rich_sha` counter gates a single post-push GET at `rich_reemit == 2`, overlaying the observed value into baseline without writing baseline, to break re-emit loops in one fetch while keeping `_advance_baselines` the sole writer.

Two distinct emit vs baseline compares must coexist: emit uses plain inbound-decoded remote; baseline's local side normalizes through `RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to match `decode(baseline_wire)`, suppressing churn on Jira-native constructs under origin-gating.

WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound must be redefined as `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` restoring the codec law; both DC create sites (backend._map_local_to_dc_fields and _issues._translate_create_fields) must route through `to_wire(fit_outbound(...))` to render on CREATE matching UPDATE, preventing comment-diff key shifts in outbound_comments._diff_comments.

The cutover flag `reconciler.rich_text_cutover` (off|cloud|dc|both) gates both send paths and defaults OFF; when absent or when marklas/pandoc extras are unavailable, codecs degrade to plain-text ADF wire without raising, restoring to rollback-identical behaviour.

Concurrent both-sides body edits remain local-wins via existing a713 mechanism, raising outbound-field-conflict alerts; baseline advances only through `_advance_baselines`, and Jira-native constructs survive edit-free passes under origin-gating.
